rationale: This is the central pydantic BaseSettings configuration for the FastAPI backend. It is loaded from the environment and the .env file, and it governs the database URL, secrets, token expiry, SMTP and Sentry settings. It also validates that default secrets have been changed. It is a significant shared configuration component, but it does not itself authenticate, persist data or integrate with external systems.

A generated TanStack Router type interface (routeTree.gen.ts) that only lists the root route's child route types. It is generated boilerplate typing, not a route or navigation graph element itself. The route tree as a whole would be the navigation graph, but this interface is not.

FastAPI router module grouping the /utils endpoints (test-email, health-check) under a shared prefix and tag. It is the API surface grouping for utility operations. Auth is delegated to a superuser dependency and email sending to helpers, so the module itself implements no cross-cutting concern.

A shadcn/ui-style reusable sidebar sub-component: a styled button primitive with a props contract and no callers. It is a library component definition in the UI kit, but it is generated-style boilerplate with minor architectural significance.

HTTP GET route handler for /users/{user_id}, an API operation contract. It enforces an access check inline (self or superuser, otherwise 403) and reads the User record from the database session. Authentication comes in through the CurrentUser dependency rather than being performed here.

SQLModel ORM entity with table=True defining the persisted User entity (id, hashed password, timestamps, items relationship). An ORM model is an object schema in the data-model layer and maps to a user table. It is a core domain entity, so it is architecturally significant.

A generated SDK client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/test-token with bearer security. The spec treats generated client methods tied to a method and path as evidence of an API operation. It makes an HTTP call to the backend but does not verify identity itself, and as generated code it has moderate significance.

A trivial TypeScript props interface for the DeleteUser React component, holding only an id and a success callback. It is an implementation detail of the component's prop typing, not an architectural element in its own right. The component itself would be modelled in the ux layer instead.

FastAPI route handler for PATCH /me/password, an HTTP operation contract. It verifies the current password credential and hashes the new one, so it implements authentication logic. It commits the updated user to the database session, so it persists data.

Private config-validation helper that rejects or warns about placeholder secret values. It is an implementation detail of the Settings class, called only by _enforce_non_default_secrets, and below model granularity. It is security hygiene but does not itself authenticate or authorize anything.

HTTP GET / route on the users router: an API operation contract listing users with skip/limit pagination. The handler queries the database directly via the session (count plus paged select), so it performs persistence. Any admin-only dependency is declared at the decorator, not in this body, so authorization is not marked.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts Axios client runtime (createClient factory). Generated boilerplate HTTP plumbing rather than a named architectural element; it performs HTTP calls (external integration) and delegates auth to setAuthParams. The generated API client as a whole might be evidence for api operations, but this runtime module itself is scaffolding.

A trivial TypeScript props interface with a single field for the ItemActionsMenu component. It is a type-level implementation detail of the UI component, not an architectural element in its own right; the component itself would be modelled in the UX layer.

Auto-generated (@hey-api/openapi-ts) path/query parameter serialization utilities for the API client. This is generated boilerplate and formatting helpers below the level an architecture model would record.

A non-table SQLModel (Pydantic) class that defines the JSON shape of the login response (access_token, token_type). Because FastAPI publishes it as a response schema, it is an object schema. It is a passive token payload and does not itself verify identity, so no concern applies. It is notable but small.

This is the root route's render function in TanStack Router. It acts as the application page shell, rendering head content, the router Outlet and developer tools. The spec treats a framework layout shell that renders an outlet as a View. It is a thin root layout with no logic of its own, so its significance is moderate.

HTTP route POST /signup is an API operation contract for public user self-registration. It checks for an existing email and creates the user via crud helpers. Persistence is delegated to crud, so the route itself does not own storage. It is a significant entry point for the user management API.

Generated client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/access-token. Per the spec, a generated client method for a distinct method and path is evidence for an api operation. It performs the OAuth2 password-form token login over HTTP to the backend. Being generated code, it is moderately significant.

A non-table SQLModel (Pydantic) class that defines the request payload for the password-reset flow: a reset token plus a new password limited to 8–128 characters. Its shape is published in the OpenAPI schema, so it is an object schema. It only carries credential data and performs no authentication itself.

A trivial shadcn/ui wrapper around the Radix Tooltip Provider that only sets a default delay. It is generated-style UI boilerplate below the granularity of a library component element. It renders UI context, but it is not an architecturally meaningful element.

Generated (.gen.ts) options type for the API client's path parameter serializer, holding only explode and style settings. It is boilerplate from code generation, an implementation detail with no architectural meaning of its own.

Skeleton loading placeholder for the users table, rendered while data loads. It is a minor UI component with no props or logic, used as a pending state for the admin users view. It is a UX element of low architectural significance.

HTTP PATCH /users/me route is an API operation contract letting the authenticated user update their own profile. It checks email uniqueness and commits changes via the session, so it does persist data. Authentication is supplied through the CurrentUser dependency rather than implemented here.

SQLModel (Pydantic) request model for self-service profile updates. Its shape is published via FastAPI/OpenAPI as a schema with field constraints (max_length, EmailStr), so it is a data-model object schema. It is not a table, and it is a notable but not central DTO.

This is a generated client method bound to PATCH /api/v1/users/me, and the API layer treats each such method-plus-path binding as evidence of an Operation. It makes the HTTP call to the backend. It only declares a bearer scheme and does not itself verify identity, so authentication is false.

A tiny generated type in an OpenAPI client path serializer (.gen.ts) that only describes the parameter shape for primitive serialization. It is generated boilerplate and an implementation detail, not an architectural element.

A shadcn/Radix design-system primitive: a reusable UI component definition with props (size, className). It belongs to the UX layer as a library component. It is a styling wrapper of minor architectural significance, sitting inside the larger Select component.

Small reusable React Email UI module exporting the Callout and Detail presentational components with inline styles. As email template building blocks they are reusable library components, but they are minor styling wrappers with no callers or logic, so their significance is low.

An HTTP GET route on /health-check/ is an API operation contract, used by load balancers and orchestrators for liveness probing. It is a trivial endpoint returning True, so its significance is moderate. Serving a health probe counts as an observability concern.

A generated OpenAPI client method bound to DELETE /api/v1/items/{id} with a bearer security requirement. The api layer counts generated client methods tied to a distinct method and path as Operation instances. It makes an HTTP call to the backend, which is the external integration concern. It does not verify identity itself, so authentication is false.

A trivial wrapper around toast.success inside the useCustomToast hook. It is widely called, but it is a UI feedback helper below modelling granularity. At most it is part of an action-pattern feedback convention, and it is not an element on its own. It does render a user-facing notification.

TanStack Router module augmentation boilerplate that registers the router type for type inference. It is a type-level declaration with no behaviour, so it is not an architectural element. The router itself would be modelled as the navigation graph.

SQLModel (Pydantic) request schema for user registration whose shape is published via OpenAPI by FastAPI; a non-table DTO with field constraints. It is modelled as a data-model object schema mapping to the signup request body. It only declares fields and does not itself authenticate or persist anything.

HTTP PATCH /me/password route handler is an API operation contract. It verifies the current password and hashes the new credential (authentication work), then commits the updated user record to the database session. It is a significant endpoint for user credential management.

Utility module bundling email composition/sending via SMTP and password-reset JWT generation/verification. It is a cohesive notification-and-token helper component rather than a single concern; it sends to an external SMTP server, issues and verifies reset tokens, and logs send results. Named by maintainers but not central.

A SQLModel (Pydantic) response model for the paginated user list, returned by read_users; FastAPI publishes its shape as an OpenAPI schema. That makes it a data-model object schema rather than a plain data object. It has no behaviour and is not persisted as a table.

Generated SDK client method bound to PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}. Per the API layer definition, a generated client method tied to one method-path pair is evidence for an Operation. It performs the HTTP call to the backend. Being generated code, it is of moderate significance.

A props type interface for the Logo UI component. It is part of that component's prop schema and is not a standalone architectural element. The Logo library component itself would be the modelled element, so this trivial type definition is an implementation detail.

FastAPI route handler for PUT /items/{id}, an HTTP operation contract. It performs an inline ownership/superuser permission check (authorization) and reads/writes the Item via the DB session (persistence). Authentication is resolved by the injected CurrentUser dependency, not by this function.

FastAPI router module defining the /private prefix with a single POST /users/ endpoint. It is part of the API surface: a route group exposing one operation. It is a dev/local-only private API grouping of moderate significance. It persists users via the session; password hashing is delegated to a security module.

SQLModel base class declaring the shared Item fields (title and description, with length constraints). The shape is published via the Pydantic/OpenAPI schema and inherited by the Item table and DTOs. It is a logical object schema rather than a table. It is notable but secondary to the Item entity itself.

An HTTP PATCH route on /users/{user_id} is an API operation contract: it updates a user, returns 404/409 responses and reads and writes the user record through the session. In the FastAPI template this route is admin-guarded by a superuser dependency at the decorator level, but the handler itself performs no auth checks.

Generated TanStack Router type-map interface in routeTree.gen.ts. It maps route paths to route types for type safety. This is generated boilerplate, not a route definition itself. The routes and the navigation graph are modelled from the route files, so this interface is not an element.

Generated SDK client method bound to POST /api/v1/items/ with bearer security. The spec treats generated client methods bound to a distinct method and path as evidence of an API operation. It issues an HTTP call to the backend, which is external integration. As generated code it duplicates the server-side contract, so significance is moderate.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive that renders a pulsing loading placeholder div. It is a generic design-system component definition with a props pass-through, so it fits ux librarycomponent. It is trivial, likely generated boilerplate used by one caller, so its significance is low.

HTTP GET /me route returning the authenticated current user; an API operation contract. Authentication is resolved by the CurrentUser dependency, not by this handler itself, so no concerns are flagged. A significant but ordinary endpoint in the users API.

A shadcn/ui-style reusable sidebar component family that defines props, context, variants and composable parts consumed across views. It is a design-system library component, essentially vendored boilerplate. Cookie storage of open state is a UI preference, not a durable data store, so persistence is not counted. Its significance is moderate as a layout building block.

A generated API client method bound to DELETE /api/v1/users/me. The spec treats each generated client method on a distinct method and path as evidence of an API Operation. It is a thin generated wrapper that issues the HTTP call. It only declares the bearer security scheme and does not verify identity itself.

Generated TanStack Router module-augmentation type declaration in routeTree.gen.ts. It mirrors the route table for type safety but is generated boilerplate. The routes themselves (and the navigation graph) would be modelled from the route files, not this interface.

Reusable styled email UI component (h1 heading wrapper) shared across three email templates. It is a small library component definition with a children prop, so it is a minor UX building block rather than a view, and it renders user-facing content.

React Email template that renders the user-facing 'new account' email with credentials and a dashboard link. It is a complete, standalone display surface built from shared UI components, so it fits ux view. It is a notable template, not core architecture. It only displays credentials and does not verify them.

A Pydantic request model defined in the private routes module, used as the request payload for the private user-creation endpoint. FastAPI publishes it in the OpenAPI document as a schema, so it is an API contract element of modest significance. It holds a password field but performs no authentication or persistence itself.

An HTTP POST /users/ route on the private router is an API operation contract. The handler writes a new User directly through the database session, so it does data persistence. It only calls the password hashing helper rather than verifying identity, so authentication is not marked. It is a significant integration point.

A generated SDK client method bound to GET /api/v1/users/ with a bearer security requirement. The api layer treats each generated client method on a distinct method and path as an Operation instance. It issues the HTTP call to the backend but does not itself verify credentials.

SQLModel/Pydantic input DTO received via the API on user creation, extending UserBase with a validated password field. Its shape is published as an OpenAPI schema, so it is a data-model object schema. It is a notable but non-core contract type, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A trivial TypeScript props interface for a sidebar component with a single items field. It is component-local typing boilerplate, not an architectural element. At most it would be an attribute of the component's prop schema.

An inline arrow function that renders a screen-reader-only 'Actions' header label for one table column definition. It is a trivial rendering detail inside the column configuration, not an architectural element on its own. It renders UI, so the user_interface concern applies.

A TanStack file route module that defines and renders the User Settings page, a routable screen composing the profile, password and delete-account tabs. It is best modelled as a UX view; the route binding is secondary. The superuser tab check is a trivial display tweak, not real authorization logic.

A private Pydantic field validator that rewrites the database URL scheme to use the psycopg driver. It is a trivial string-normalisation helper inside the settings class. It does not touch storage itself, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

A non-table SQLModel that serves as the paginated response wrapper for read_items (a list of ItemPublic plus a count). FastAPI publishes its shape in the OpenAPI schema, so it is modelled as an object schema. It is a minor collection DTO rather than a core entity, hence moderate significance.

A shadcn/ui-style reusable UI primitive wrapping the Radix Avatar Fallback with styling. It is a reusable library component definition in the design system. It is a thin styling wrapper with low significance, but it does render UI.

A props type for the EditUser React component, holding only a user object and a success callback. It is an implementation detail of the component's prop contract, not an architectural element in its own right; the EditUser component itself would be the modelled UX element.

An HTTP POST route handler bound to /password-recovery-html-content/{email}, so it is an API operation. It is part of the password-recovery (authentication) flow: it issues a reset token and returns a preview of the recovery email HTML. It is an auxiliary admin/debug endpoint, not a core boundary, so significance is moderate.

This module only holds a trivial React hook that detects a mobile viewport breakpoint via matchMedia. It is a generic UI utility (shadcn-style boilerplate) with no architectural responsibility, so it is not a modelled element. It does drive UI responsiveness, so user_interface is set.

HTTP POST /test-email/ route is an API operation contract. It is a utility/diagnostic endpoint for sending a test email, which makes it a notable but non-core part of the API surface. Email sending is delegated to send_email, so the route itself does not implement the external integration.

Generated API client method bound to POST /api/v1/reset-password/. The operation definition explicitly counts generated client methods as evidence of an Operation. It is a thin generated wrapper, so its significance is moderate. It makes an HTTP call to the backend but does not itself verify credentials.

Trivial React props interface declaring only a children slot for the AuthLayout component. It is boilerplate typing for a UI component, not an architectural element itself; the AuthLayout component would be modelled instead, with this interface at most an attribute of it.

SQLModel (pydantic) update DTO whose shape is published as a request schema via FastAPI/OpenAPI. It declares typed, constrained fields, so it is an object schema in the data model. It is a notable but non-core variant of the Item entity.

FastAPI route handler for PATCH /users/{user_id}, defining an HTTP operation contract with 404/409 responses. It reads the user via the session and persists the update through the crud layer. The route decorator (likely superuser-dependent) is not shown, so authorization is not attributed to the function body.

This is a small React hook that wraps sonner toasts with standard success and error feedback messages. It is a reusable UI feedback convention, so ActionPattern is the closest fit. It is a thin wrapper, so significance is low. It does render user-facing notifications.

HTTP DELETE route on users (/users/{user_id}) is an API operation contract. The handler deletes the user and their items via the DB session, so it does data persistence. It also performs a self-deletion check that returns 403, which is authorization logic. Superuser gating likely comes from a router dependency.

SQLModel ORM entity (table=True) defining the persisted Item record, with its primary key, timestamp and owner foreign key. Per the spec, an ORM model is a data-model object schema that maps to its data-store collection. It is a core domain entity that declares durable storage shape.

Generated (types.gen.ts) TypeScript type for the hey-api HTTP client's request options. It is boilerplate scaffolding of a generated API client, not an architectural element. It only declares fields and performs no auth, I/O or integration itself.

A generated client method bound to POST /api/v1/password-recovery/{email}. The spec counts each generated client method on a distinct method and path as one Operation instance. It makes an HTTP call to the backend. It is generated and thin, but it records the password-recovery endpoint contract the frontend consumes.

A trivial route option that returns static page-title metadata for the reset-password route. It is boilerplate configuration below architectural granularity. At most it is a detail of the route meta, not an element on its own.

Module creates the SQLModel engine bound to DATABASE_URL, which is the application's single database connection point. It also seeds the first superuser. This makes it the evidence for the persistence deployment the app connects to, so it is modelled as a data-store Database element of real architectural significance.

HTTP route POST /password-recovery/{email} is an API operation contract. It drives the credential recovery flow by generating a reset token and triggering a reset email, so it implements authentication. It delegates user lookup and email sending to helpers, so no persistence or integration concern is marked. It is a significant system boundary endpoint.

SQLModel (Pydantic) request schema for user updates. Its shape is published via the FastAPI OpenAPI spec and carries field constraints, so it is an object schema rather than a plain data object. It is a notable DTO in the user model family but is not a persisted table.

Generated client method bound to GET /api/v1/users/me with a bearer security requirement. Per the api layer rules it is evidence for that operation. Its callers use it to establish the current user. Because it is generated code, it is moderately significant. It makes an HTTP call to the backend but does not verify identity itself.

Generated API-client boilerplate: an empty type-composition interface for path parameter serialization options. It is an implementation detail of the generated client, not an architectural element. It has no callers or behaviour and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Routable page component rendering the password recovery screen with an email form that triggers the recover-password API call. It is a top-level UI surface (view) in the authentication flow, so it carries both user-interface and authentication (credential recovery) concerns.

HTTP route DELETE /users/me is an API operation contract letting a user delete their own account. It enforces a check (superusers cannot self-delete, returns 403) and deletes the user via the DB session. Authentication is provided by the CurrentUser dependency, not implemented here.

React module defining the Edit Item modal dialog: a dropdown menu trigger opens a form with zod validation, which submits via ItemsService.updateItem. A modal dialog is a standalone UI surface, so it is a ux view. It renders UI but only calls the API client rather than implementing integration itself. Notable but not core.

This is a generated SDK client method bound to POST /api/v1/private/users/, and the spec counts generated client methods tied to a distinct method and path as API operations. It issues an HTTP call to the backend. The private user-creation endpoint is notable but secondary, and the method is generated with no callers, so significance is moderate.

A simple dataclass carrying an email's HTML content and subject between the email generators and the sender. It is a passive in-code data carrier, neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject of minor significance.

A props type declaration for the DataTable component (columns and data). It is part of the library component's prop schema, which is an attribute of ux.librarycomponent DataTable, not an element in its own right. This is trivial typing boilerplate.

A private Pydantic model validator that defaults EMAILS_FROM_NAME to PROJECT_NAME inside the Settings class. It is a trivial configuration-defaulting helper below the granularity of an architecture element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A shadcn-style reusable Input primitive with a prop schema, used across several views (login, signup, recover password, sidebar). This makes it a UX library component. It is a generic styled wrapper around the native input element, so its architectural significance is low.

HTTP POST route /login/test-token is an API operation contract. It validates the bearer token through the CurrentUser dependency and returns the authenticated user. It is a minor utility endpoint for token verification, notable but not core.

Frontend bootstrap entry point. It mounts the React SPA root and sets the app-wide theme provider, router and query client. It configures the API client with a bearer token taken from localStorage, and on a 401/403 response it clears that token and redirects to the login page. It is the deployable front-end app root, so it is modelled as a UXApplication.

Generated TanStack Router type declaration (routeTree.gen.ts) listing route path literals for type safety. It is generated boilerplate, not a route or navigation graph element itself. The routes it enumerates would be modelled from the route files, not from this type.

CardTitle is a shadcn-style UI primitive, a reusable library component that renders a styled div. It belongs in the UX layer as a library component. It is a trivial sub-part of the Card component and would rarely be modelled on its own, so significance is low.

File-based route module defining the /signup page: a routable screen composing an auth layout and a signup form, with a beforeLoad redirect guard. The module is best modelled as the Sign Up view. Registration is delegated to useAuth, so the module itself performs no authentication or persistence; it renders the UI.

HTTP POST /reset-password/ route is an API operation contract. It verifies a password reset token (credential handling, authentication) and updates the user's password via the CRUD layer (persistence). It is a significant boundary endpoint in the auth flow.

A TanStack Router generated type mapping full paths to route types in routeTree.gen.ts. It is generated boilerplate. The route table it reflects would be modelled as a navigation graph and its routes, not this type-level helper interface.

A CRUD-layer query that selects a User by email from the database, issued by application code. This fits a data-store access pattern: a single read keyed on email against the user collection. It is widely used by login and user routes, so it is notable but not core.

A settings validator that rejects default values for SECRET_KEY, the database password and the superuser password. It is a security control against weak or default credentials, best modelled as a countermeasure. It is a narrow, private config check, so its significance is modest. It verifies no identity itself, so no concern flag applies.

A trivial computed property on the Settings configuration class that returns whether the SMTP host and from-address are both set. It is a derived accessor and an implementation detail, so it is not an architectural element on its own.

Reusable sidebar main-navigation menu component that takes items via props and renders router links with active-state highlighting. It is a UI building block embedded in the app layout, not a route table, so it is a ux librarycomponent of moderate significance.

HTTP PUT route on items path is an API operation contract. The handler performs an ownership/superuser permission check, which counts as authorization, and reads and writes the Item via the DB session. Authentication is handled by the CurrentUser dependency rather than by this handler.

Generic request-shape type in a generated API client (types.gen.ts). It is boilerplate scaffolding for the generated HTTP client, not an API contract or domain schema, so it is not an architectural element on its own.

This is a generated TanStack Router routeTree.gen.ts arrow function that returns the parent LayoutRoute. It is code-generated boilerplate wiring the route hierarchy. The routes themselves are navigation elements, but this accessor is not an architectural element on its own.

Frontend authentication hook: performs login via the API, stores and removes the access token in localStorage, handles signup and logout, and fetches the current user. It is the client's central identity mechanism, so it is best modelled as the security layer's authentication configuration and is architecturally significant.

A shadcn/ui styling wrapper around the Radix DropdownMenu SubContent primitive. It is generated-style boilerplate that only adds class names and has no callers. It renders UI, but it sits below the granularity of a library component element; at most it is part of the DropdownMenu library component.

A TypeScript props interface for the DeleteItem React component, holding only an id and a success callback. It is part of the component's signature rather than a standalone architectural element. The DeleteItem component itself would be the UX element, so this falls below the modelling granularity.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client utility module (query serialization, auth param injection, URL building). Generated boilerplate below the granularity of an architecture element. The generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this helper module is not.

POST /users/ is an HTTP route handler, so it is an API operation contract for creating a user. It is a meaningful system boundary. It delegates persistence to crud functions and email delivery to send_email; it only checks for duplicate emails and orchestrates those calls.

POST /login/access-token is an HTTP operation contract, the OAuth2 token endpoint. It verifies credentials and active status and issues a JWT, making it a core authentication entry point at the system boundary. Persistence is delegated to crud.authenticate, so the endpoint itself does not touch storage.

A generated (auth.gen.ts) type in the API client core that describes how auth credentials are attached to requests. It is generated boilerplate mirroring the OpenAPI security scheme shape. It has no callers and no behaviour, so it sits below the modelling threshold.

HTTP route handler for POST /login/access-token, an OAuth2 password-flow token endpoint. It is an API operation and a system entry point. It performs authentication itself by validating credentials, checking the user is active and issuing a JWT. Persistence is delegated to crud.

A React component with a destructive menu entry that opens a confirm dialog and calls ItemsService.deleteItem. It is a user-operable trigger that starts the delete-item API operation, so it is a UX action component. It is a notable but local UI unit. The API call goes through the generated client and is not itself an integration.

A props type for a UI password input component that only extends the native input props with an optional error string. It is a trivial type declaration supporting the library component, not an architectural element in its own right. Any modelling belongs on the PasswordInput component itself.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts helper module that serializes query key values into JSON-friendly shapes for Pinia Colada caching. It is generated boilerplate and a formatting utility, not an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A React full-screen 404 page component rendered as the router's not-found surface. It is a standalone top-level UI screen, so it is a UX view. It is notable but not central: it contains only static markup and a link back to the home route.

This is a generated (.gen.ts) configuration type for the OpenAPI-generated HTTP client. It is boilerplate scaffolding with no callers in the graph and holds only an auth token slot, not authentication logic. It sits below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not modelled as an element.

A reusable shadcn/ui Sidebar primitive with a prop schema (side, variant, collapsible) and a children slot. It renders responsive desktop and mobile layouts and is instantiated by AppSidebar. That makes it a design-system library component: a notable UI building block, but generic scaffolding rather than an app-specific screen.

FastAPI application entry point: constructs the app, wires CORS, mounts the API router and frontend, and initializes Sentry tracing. It is the backend's deployable root component and system boundary, so it is a core application component rather than a single API contract.

Generated (types.gen.ts) configuration type for the hey-api Axios client, holding options such as baseURL, headers and throwOnError. It is generated boilerplate with no callers and no architectural identity of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

React component rendering an admin 'Edit User' modal dialog with a form, triggered from a dropdown menu item. It submits via the generated UsersService client. It is a standalone modal surface, so it is modelled as a ux view. It is a notable admin screen but not core to the architecture.

FastAPI router module defining the /items CRUD endpoints. It is an API surface grouping operations under the items path. It performs ownership/superuser permission checks and reads and writes the database via the session. The individual route handlers are the operations, and this module groups them as the path-level API element.

A trivial local wrapper inside the DeleteItem component that forwards to the generated ItemsService.deleteItem client call. It is an implementation detail of the component's mutation, not an architectural element on its own. The external call is made by the generated SDK, not by this wrapper.

Generated TanStack Router type map (routeTree.gen.ts) keyed by route ID. It is boilerplate typing scaffolding produced by the router plugin, not a route or navigation graph element itself. The routes it lists would be modelled from their own definitions.

A shadcn-style styled div wrapper for a dialog footer. It is generated boilerplate design-system scaffolding with no props schema or behaviour of its own, so it falls below the granularity of a UX element. It does render UI markup.

Module defining the admin users table's column configuration (headers, field bindings, cell rendering, actions column). In the UX layer this is table column configuration for a table component instance. It is a notable UI unit within the admin view but not core architecture.

Generated client boilerplate (.gen.ts) defining the generic shape of a server-sent event message. It is a low-level transport type in an auto-generated API client with no callers or domain meaning, below the granularity of an architectural element.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client core helper that maps call arguments into body/headers/path/query slots. It is generated boilerplate and an implementation detail of the API client, not an architectural element on its own.

Small utility that reads an email template file and renders it with Jinja2. It is a formatting helper used by the email-generation functions, sitting below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. Reading a bundled template is not durable data persistence.

Vite build configuration file: a build/deployment configuration artifact that defines the frontend bundle output into the backend directory and its plugins. It is infrastructure evidence rather than application logic, and has low standalone architectural significance.

A small options interface inside a generated API client's path serializer (pathSerializer.gen.ts). It is generated boilerplate and a parameter-serialization implementation detail, so it is not an architecturally meaningful element and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A TypeScript props interface for the EditItem React component. It is an implementation detail of the component's prop signature, with no callers or behaviour of its own. It would be captured as an attribute of the EditItem UX element, not as a separate architecture element.

FastAPI route handler for POST /login/test-token. It is an API operation that validates the bearer token through the CurrentUser dependency and returns the authenticated user. This is a minor auth-checking endpoint in the login router, not a test suite.

Thin styled wrapper over the react-email Link component, exported from a shared email UI package for reuse across email templates. It is a reusable UI component definition with a props contract (href, children), but it is trivial and has low architectural significance on its own.

This is a shadcn/ui-style Tabs component module that wraps Radix primitives with styling. It is a reusable UI library component definition, so it belongs to ux as a librarycomponent. It is largely generated boilerplate of low architectural significance, but it does render user interface.

A small type in a generated API client utility file (utils.gen.ts) that describes the path-parameter and URL inputs for path serialization. It is generated boilerplate and an internal implementation detail, not an architecturally meaningful element. Nothing calls it.

A shadcn-style UI primitive wrapper rendering the sheet backdrop overlay with styling classes. It is a reusable library component piece in the design-system folder, used internally by SheetContent. It renders UI but is a minor, mostly boilerplate building block.

A trivial props interface declaring two optional fields for a sidebar user-info component. It is an implementation detail of a UI component, not a component itself, so it falls below the granularity of an architecture model element.

A shadcn/ui-style Checkbox module that wraps the Radix primitive. It is a reusable UI library component definition with props passthrough, which makes it a ux librarycomponent. It is generated boilerplate primitive of minor architectural significance, and it only renders UI.

FastAPI route handler for POST /password-recovery/{email}, which makes it an API operation. It is part of the credential-recovery flow: it issues a password reset token and triggers the reset email, so it implements authentication behaviour. Persistence and email sending are delegated to its callees, so neither concern is flagged.

React component rendering the sidebar's user menu (user info, settings link, logout action). It is a non-routable fragment placed inside AppSidebar that composes several library component instances, so it is a UX subview. Logout is delegated to useAuth, so it does not implement authentication itself.

A generated type (params.gen.ts) in an API client's core plumbing, describing how parameter fields map to request slots. It is generated boilerplate and an implementation detail with no callers, so it does not qualify as an architectural element.

A React 404 page component rendered as a standalone screen when no route matches (the router's notFoundComponent). It is a top-level UI surface with a 'Go Back' link, so it is a UX view. It is a notable but generic fallback screen.

Generated (.gen.ts) API client options interface with only baseURL and throwOnError fields. It is boilerplate configuration typing from an OpenAPI client generator, below the granularity of an architectural element, and has no callers or behaviour.

A trivial shadcn/ui wrapper around a Radix Sheet trigger primitive that only adds a data-slot attribute. It is generated design-system boilerplate rather than an architecturally meaningful UI component. It renders UI, but it is below modelling granularity.

Auto-generated barrel module from @hey-api/openapi-ts that only re-exports client helpers and types. It is generated boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, below modelling granularity. The generated API client itself, rather than this index file, would be the API-layer evidence.

A shadcn/Radix wrapper primitive for avatar images in the UI component library. It is a reusable library component definition with props, but it is a thin styling wrapper and a minor element within the design system, so it has low significance.

A React Email template that renders the password-reset email, a complete user-facing surface built from shared UI components (Layout, Heading, LinkButton). It is best modelled as a UX view. It only presents the reset link and does not verify credentials itself. It is a notable template within the email package.

A trivial TypeScript props interface with a single field for the UserActionsMenu component. It is an implementation detail of the component's prop typing, not an architectural element on its own. The component itself would be modelled in ux, but this props type is boilerplate.

A props type for a shadcn-style UI button component. It is a typing detail of the LoadingButton library component, not an architectural element in its own right. The component itself would be modelled as ux.librarycomponent, with this interface as its prop schema attribute.

Inline arrow function in the API client configuration that supplies the bearer token from localStorage. It is a small piece of authentication wiring rather than a standalone element, but it is evidence for the frontend's token-based authentication configuration. It reads browser storage, which counts as persistence.

This module is a shadcn/ui Badge primitive: a reusable, generic UI component definition with variant props, and it is not a screen. It is a library component in the UX layer. Its significance is low because it is generated design-system boilerplate with no callers recorded.

Generated API-client boilerplate (params.gen.ts) defining an internal parameter bucket type for request building. It is generated scaffolding below architectural granularity, not an API contract or domain schema, and is not referenced by any callers.

A trivial shadcn-style styled span wrapper for keyboard shortcut text inside a dropdown menu. It is generated/boilerplate UI primitive scaffolding below the granularity of a library component element; it renders UI, but is not architecturally meaningful on its own.

A shadcn-style reusable Button definition with variant and size props in the UI components library. It is a generic design-system component with a props schema, not a specific action control. It is a library component of moderate significance and renders UI.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive that renders the pagination ellipsis. It is a generic design-system subcomponent in the ui library, not a screen, so it is a minor library component with low significance. It renders user-facing UI.

This is the central application configuration module. It loads environment settings through pydantic-settings and exposes a singleton used across the backend. It defines settings for the database, SMTP, Sentry and secrets, and validates against default secrets. It is a cross-cutting configuration component rather than an infrastructure or security element, and it does not itself perform auth, persistence or integration work.

This is a shadcn/ui-style wrapper around the Radix Checkbox primitive: a reusable design-system component definition with a props schema that is styled and exported for use across views. It is a generic library primitive, likely generated boilerplate, so its architectural significance is low.

Alembic migration downgrade step that reverts UUID primary keys back to integer IDs on the user and item tables, rebuilding sequences, PKs and FKs. It is schema migration evidence for the data-store layer, but a single direction of one migration is a minor unit. No element type fits a migration directly, so element_type is null.

TanStack file-route module binding '/recover-password' to the RecoverPassword view with a beforeLoad redirect for logged-in users. As a router entry it is a navigation Route. It also renders the recovery form, so it drives UI. It only calls the API client and does not itself verify credentials.

A React Email template that renders a complete, standalone user-facing email surface (the test-delivery email) from library components such as Layout, Heading and Callout. It is best modelled as a UX view: a top-level display unit. It is notable but not central, since it only confirms that email delivery works.

A trivial TanStack Router head() callback returning static page-title metadata for the dashboard route. It is a configuration detail of the route rather than an architectural element on its own. At most it could be folded into route meta as an attribute.

Playwright end-to-end test configuration: it sets the test directory, retries, reporters, browser projects, an auth setup dependency and the dev web server. It is testing-layer evidence for the E2E test environment, but no listed coverage-model element type fits a runner config. It is notable for test infrastructure, not core architecture.

Alembic migration altering column lengths on the user and item tables. It is physical schema evolution, so it belongs to the data-store layer. No data-store element type models a migration itself; it is evidence for the field elements it changes. It is a notable but routine schema change.

Small UI cell renderer in the Items table columns that displays an ID and offers a copy-to-clipboard button. It is a user-operable control, so it is UX, but it is a minor table-cell detail with low architectural significance.

TanStack file-route module that binds /reset-password to the ResetPassword view. It validates the token search parameter and runs a beforeLoad guard that redirects logged-in users or token-less requests. The view renders the password-reset form, part of the credential recovery flow, so the route entry is the defining element.

Cookiecutter post-generation hook script that normalizes CRLF line endings to LF in generated shell scripts. This is project-scaffolding boilerplate with no architectural role. It does rewrite files on disk, which counts as trivial data persistence.

Logout ends the client session by removing the stored access token from localStorage and redirecting to /login. It is authentication session logic inside the useAuth hook, but it is a small function, and no security element type fits a logout action precisely. Notable to maintainers, not a standalone component.

Core security module fixing the authentication mechanism: JWT access-token issuance (HS256 with the secret key) and Argon2/bcrypt password hashing and verification. It defines how principals prove identity, not what they may do, so it maps to an AuthenticationConfig and is architecturally significant.

Inline mutation success callback inside the ChangePassword component: shows a toast and resets the form. It is a trivial UI feedback detail below the level a maintainer would name, not an architectural element on its own. It does drive user-facing UI feedback.

Shadcn-style generated wrapper that only applies styling classes to a Radix Dialog.Description primitive. It is boilerplate UI scaffolding below architectural granularity. It renders UI but is not a meaningful library component on its own. The Dialog composite would be the modelled element, if anything.

FastAPI dependency module defining the OAuth2 bearer scheme, JWT decoding to resolve the current user, a superuser privilege check, and the DB session provider. It is primarily the application's authentication mechanism (token-based identity verification) with a role check, used across all protected routes.

This FastAPI router module defines the /users API surface: ten operations covering CRUD, signup, self-service and password changes. It is best modelled as an API grouping of operations under the users path. It does auth work itself (password verification and hashing, superuser dependencies), writes to the database, and sends email.

An anonymous cell renderer inside a table column definition that wraps UserActionsMenu in a div. It is a trivial rendering detail below architectural granularity. The column configuration or the menu component might be modelled, but this callback on its own would not be.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive wrapping the Radix Avatar root with styling. It is a reusable library component definition in the design system, but a thin generated-style wrapper of minor architectural significance. It renders UI.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts helper module providing request body serializers (FormData, JSON, URLSearchParams). Generated boilerplate and serialization utilities fall below architectural granularity. The generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this internal serialization file is not an element on its own.

A reusable shadcn-style UI library component, a button that toggles the sidebar. It belongs to the UX layer as a library component definition, accepts Button props and is used by the layout. It is generated-style UI kit code of minor architectural significance.

The initial Alembic migration creates the user and item tables, with their columns, primary keys, a unique email index and the owner foreign key. It is direct evidence of the physical schema, best modelled as the collections it defines. It writes durable schema, so data persistence is true.

Build-tooling configuration file for the OpenAPI TypeScript client generator. It is a configuration artifact that drives code generation and is not runtime application logic. It is minor architecturally: at most a technology artifact that a maintainer might note as the source of the generated API client.

A React confirmation dialog in user settings. It renders a 'Delete Account' trigger and a modal with Cancel and Delete actions, and on confirm calls UsersService.deleteUserMe and then logout. It is best modelled as a modal view surface with its own open/close lifecycle. The API call and logout are delegated to other code, not implemented here.

shadcn/ui form primitives module wrapping react-hook-form and Radix (FormItem, FormLabel, FormControl). It is a reusable UI library component definition, but it is generated design-system boilerplate with low architectural significance. It renders the user interface.

A thin React wrapper that renders a Suspense boundary, showing a pending skeleton while ItemsTableContent loads. It is a minor, non-routable UI fragment inside the Items view, with little logic of its own beyond the loading fallback. It renders UI, so user_interface is true.

The CRUD module is the repository/DAO layer of the FastAPI template. It issues SQLModel session reads and writes against the User and Item tables, and it also implements credential authentication, with password hashing and timing-attack protection. As the persistence access layer it is evidence for data-store access patterns and is architecturally significant.

Auto-generated TypeScript type module produced by @hey-api/openapi-ts from the backend OpenAPI spec. Its types mirror API schemas already modelled at the source, so the module is generated boilerplate rather than an architectural element. At most it is evidence for API schemas.

Inline react-query mutation callback that only invalidates the query cache after the delete-user mutation settles. It is a trivial implementation detail inside the DeleteUser component, not an architectural element in its own right.

Standard Alembic env.py boilerplate generated by the migration tool template. It configures the migration context for offline SQL script generation. It is scaffolding for the migration runner rather than a migration or schema element itself, so it is not modelled as a node.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts core type definitions (HttpMethod, Client, Config, OmitNever) for the generated HTTP client. This is generated boilerplate scaffolding with no callers and no domain meaning, so it is not an architectural element. Its auth field is only a type declaration and does not itself verify identity.

A shadcn-style reusable Input primitive in the UI component library. It accepts props and renders a styled input, so it is a library component definition. It is largely generated boilerplate styling with low architectural significance on its own.

A trivial shadcn/ui styling wrapper around the Radix Select separator primitive. It is generated-style boilerplate with no callers and is below the granularity of a modelled library component. It does render UI, but it is not an architectural element on its own.

A shadcn/Radix-style styled wrapper for a dropdown checkbox item in the UI component library. It is a reusable library component definition with props, but it is a minor sub-part of the dropdown menu primitive with no callers, so it has low architectural significance. It renders UI.

A thin wrapper that opens a database session and delegates to init_db for seeding initial data. It is bootstrap scaffolding below the model's granularity. The actual persistence work is done by init_db, not by this function, so it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Auto-generated type definitions from @hey-api/openapi-ts for the axios HTTP client runtime (config, request options, result types). This is generated boilerplate scaffolding below the level an architecture model records; it only declares types and performs no integration itself.

A trivial shadcn/ui wrapper that forwards props to the Radix DropdownMenu Portal primitive. It is generated-style boilerplate with no callers, below the granularity of a library component element. It renders UI, but it is not architecturally meaningful on its own.

A shadcn-style UI primitive module exporting styled table wrapper components. It is a reusable library component in the design system but is largely generated boilerplate, so its architectural significance is low. It renders UI and has no other concerns.

TanStack Router's generated route tree is the app's complete client-side route table. It wires the root, layout, login, signup, password-recovery, admin, items and settings routes into one hierarchy. Although the file is generated, it is the canonical evidence for the single navigation graph rather than a trivial helper.

Inline react-query mutation callback in the EditUser dialog that only invalidates the cached 'users' query. It is a trivial implementation detail of the component's mutation configuration, not an architectural element in its own right.

Frontend utility module with trivial helpers: extracting error messages from Axios errors and computing name initials. These are formatting/helper functions below the granularity of an architectural element, so the module is not modelled.

A React component that renders the items table region, or an empty state, inside the Items page. It is a non-routable fragment that places a DataTable library component, so it fits a subview. It is a minor internal piece of the page. It fetches data through query options but does no persistence itself.

This module is a shadcn/ui-generated wrapper around the sonner Toaster that applies theme-aware icons and styling. It is a reusable UI library component taking props, but it is mostly boilerplate scaffolding from the component kit. That gives it low significance; it renders UI.

A shadcn-style sidebar primitive that wraps Input and adds styling. It is a reusable UI library component, but it is trivial and unused (no callers), so its significance is minor. It renders UI and implements no other concern.

This is a shadcn-style generated UI primitive that wraps Radix Tooltip. It is a reusable library component definition with props and slots, so it belongs to the UX layer as a librarycomponent. As near-boilerplate design-system scaffolding, its architectural significance is low.

Inline header renderer for an admin table's actions column, returning a screen-reader-only label. It is a trivial presentational lambda inside a column definition. As an implementation detail below the granularity of a table column element, it is not modelled; it does render UI text.
